question.text: Scenario: Nirmala Sundarajan is the newly appointed Compliance Officer (a qualified Company Secretary) of Pinnacle Industries Ltd., a listed entity with a market capitalization of Rs.8,500 crore and 1.2 lakh shareholders. The company is listed on both NSE and BSE. The current quarter ending is September 30, 2025. Pinnacle's Board of Directors is scheduled to meet on October 20, 2025, to consider the quarterly financial results and an interim dividend. On October 5, 2025, the company completes a preferential allotment that results in capital restructuring causing a change of more than 2% in the total paid-up share capital. The company's wholly-owned subsidiary, Pinnacle Solutions Pvt. Ltd. (which contributes 35% of consolidated revenue), is considering selling a manufacturing unit worth Rs.200 crore, representing 25% of its total assets. Nirmala must ensure all SEBI LODR compliance requirements are met while coordinating with DataServe RTAs, the company's appointed registrar and share transfer agent. DataServe manages 2.8 crore folios across all its clients and has had the same internal auditor for the past 4 years. Question 2 of 5: The preferential allotment on October 5, 2025 results in capital restructuring with a change of more than 2% in the total paid-up share capital. Under SEBI LODR, what additional filing obligation does this trigger for Nirmala?

answer.text: No additional filing since the regular quarterly filing will cover this change
A revised shareholding pattern must be filed within 10 days (by October 15, 2025) because capital restructuring resulted in a change exceeding 2% of total paid-up share capital
An immediate filing within 24 hours as a material event disclosure
A special filing within 30 days to SEBI's corporate finance department

explanation.text: The Logic: Under Regulation 31, when a capital restructuring results in a change of more than 2% in the total paid-up share capital, the listed entity must file a revised shareholding pattern within 10 days of the change. The October 5, 2025 event satisfies this trigger, so the filing is due by October 15, 2025. The Trap: The 2% trigger is measured against the total paid-up share capital, not just promoter shareholding percentage. The regular quarterly shareholding pattern filing does not subsume this separate 10-day obligation, and the 24-hour material-event window applies to a different category of disclosures. Note: Regulation 31 filings can be triggered (a) on a quarterly cycle, (b) one day prior to listing, and (c) within 10 days of any capital restructuring that changes total paid-up share capital by more than 2%. This scenario tests the third trigger.
